nodes.label: README
nodes.rationale: Reads pre-generated CSVs from data/ so the app can run without live ABS/RBA refresh; uses local system fonts and bslib-native dark/light mode to avoid third-party font fetches during launch or deployment.

nodes.label: National Affordability Score Review Memo
nodes.rationale: Ownership-channel overlap between mortgage serviceability and deposit barrier accepted for v1 because they capture distinct constraints (monthly servicing vs upfront deposit accumulation); fixed 40/35/25 weights retained; price-to-income/real wage/real rate kept out of headline to avoid double-counting.

nodes.label: Feature Review 2026-05-31
nodes.rationale: Dashboard should lead with official SIH/NHHA burden evidence beside the stylised market-entry score rather than below it; price/supply/labour/migration features kept as context not headline affordability measures.

nodes.label: National Affordability Score Methodology Spec
nodes.rationale: Score uses sparse dimension-level weights (40/35/25) rather than all available indicators because deposit gap and price-to-income correlate 0.998, which would double-count house prices; arithmetic mean chosen for v1 for explainability with geometric aggregation as a robustness check.

nodes.label: Mortgage Serviceability
nodes.rationale: Annual principal-and-interest repayments divided by annual household income at current prices and rates; 40 per cent weight in score; v1 proxy uses AWE/WPI-based serviceability. Core market-entry ownership servicing channel.

nodes.label: Rental Entry Affordability
nodes.rationale: Rent price index divided by household income index; 35 per cent weight; v1 proxy uses CPI rents divided by WPI. May understate new-lease stress because v1 uses public index-style inputs rather than a new-tenancy rent series.

nodes.label: Deposit Barrier
nodes.rationale: Deposit required divided by annual savings capacity; 25 per cent weight; v1 proxy uses deposit gap years with fixed 15 per cent savings rate and SIH-base price. Upfront ownership barrier.

nodes.label: Deposit Gap (Years)
nodes.rationale: Median dwelling price vs median household income, expressed as years to save a deposit. Correlates 0.998 with price-to-income in current data, so price-to-income is excluded from the headline score to avoid double-counting.

nodes.label: 30/40 Rule (Housing Stress)
nodes.rationale: Households in the bottom 40 per cent of equivalised disposable income distribution paying more than 30 per cent of income on housing are in housing stress. Basis of the Australian housing-stress convention from ABS SIH.

nodes.label: Housing Cost Burden
nodes.rationale: Housing costs as a percentage of gross/disposable household income.

nodes.label: NHHA Rental Affordability / Lower-Income Renter Stress
nodes.rationale: Lower-income renter households paying more than 30 per cent of gross income on rent (National Housing and Homelessness Agreement basis). Official observed-burden benchmark, a distinct concept from the market-entry score; validation only.
nodes.norm_label: nhha rental affordability / lower-income renter stress

nodes.label: Price-to-Income Ratio
nodes.rationale: Broad ownership affordability proxy (RPPI/WPI). Diagnostic/fallback only; excluded from headline score due to very high correlation with deposit gap and omission of interest rates.

nodes.label: Equivalised Disposable Income
nodes.rationale: Income adjusted for household size/composition using the modified OECD scale; basis for the bottom-40-per-cent grouping in the 30/40 rule.

nodes.label: Residual-Income Approach
nodes.rationale: Affordability should reflect income left after housing costs to meet non-housing necessities (AHURI). Stronger welfare concept than ratio thresholds; future extension, not a headline-score input.

nodes.label: Composite Indicator Methodology (OECD/JRC)
nodes.rationale: OECD/JRC handbook framework: theoretical framework, normalisation, weighting as value judgements, robustness and sensitivity testing, component decomposition. Weights are judgement weights not causal estimates.

nodes.label: NZ CHAI (Change in Housing Affordability Indicators)
nodes.author: NZ HUD
nodes.rationale: Closest conceptual analogue: measures change in affordability for renting, saving a deposit, and servicing a mortgage, each vs median household disposable income. Change indicator, not absolute level.
nodes.norm_label: nz chai (change in housing affordability indicators)

nodes.label: NAR Housing Affordability Index
nodes.author: NAR
nodes.rationale: Index of 100 = median-income family has exactly enough income to qualify for a mortgage on a median-priced home with 20 per cent down.

nodes.label: RBA RDP 2023-01 Credit Constraints
nodes.author: RBA
nodes.rationale: Credit constraints affect prices through marginal buyers not average households; financing conditions and prices jointly determined. Justifies keeping credit variables as scenario/context only.

nodes.label: Harvard JCHS 30 Percent Standard
nodes.author: Harvard JCHS
nodes.rationale: 30 per cent standard is imperfect and can overstate burden but remains useful as a simple indicator over time and across markets.

nodes.label: ABS RAID/MAID Census Affordability Indicators
nodes.author: ABS
nodes.rationale: Classify households by whether rent/mortgage exceeds 30 per cent of imputed income; ABS cautions payments above 30 per cent do not necessarily imply financial stress.

nodes.label: renv Project Environments Index
nodes.rationale: renv 1.2.0 help index; dependency tooling for project-local R environments (restore, snapshot, lockfile).
